proof: Concepts, questions and a plan before it builds
ISO screws, nuts, inserts and material fits built in
Checked for your printer after every change
Your Claude or ChatGPT plan, or a local model

steps.title: Describe it
steps.text: Say what the part is for, in words, with a sketch or a photo. Add the real sizes of the things it has to fit.

steps.title: Decide together
steps.text: The assistant offers concepts, asks what it cannot know and shows a plan. Nothing is built until you press Go.

steps.title: Check and print
steps.text: It builds editable CAD while you watch, checks the part against your printer and material, and opens it in your slicer.

tour.title: Work it out in conversation
tour.text: Say what the part is for. The assistant offers two or three concepts based on proven designs, asks about loads, cables and the real sizes of your things, and looks up data sheets with sources.
tour.alt: A conversation: fit this housing to the circuit board, answered questions, research on M3 screws per ISO 4762 and ISO 273, and the screw seated as a standard part

tour.title: It asks before it guesses
tour.text: Questions come as cards with the recommended answer preselected and its reason. Before it builds, it checks the function and shows a plan. Nothing changes until you press Go.
tour.alt: A housing in the 3D view next to questions from the assistant with recommended options

tour.title: Watch every step in real CAD
tour.text: SolidCraft builds editable geometry while you watch. Click a face, pin a note to it and ask for the change in words. Every step, yours or the assistant’s, can be taken back.
tour.alt: A cable clip with a selected face and its name, area and actions

tour.title: Add the details that make it print
tour.text: Threads, countersinks, snap fits, screw bosses, lids with a lip, seats for heat-set inserts and nut traps, sized to the standards below and placed on the face you pick.
tour.alt: The function block panel adding a heat-set insert seat for M3

tour.title: Know it will print before you slice
tour.text: After every change, PartBuddy checks the part against your printer and material and points at each finding. The assistant sees the result too.
tour.alt: The ready-to-print check reporting that lid and case are too tight

tour.title: Straight to your slicer
tour.text: Open the part in Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer with one click, or export 3MF, STEP and STL. Supports and orientation stay with your slicer.
tour.alt: The export menu with 3MF, STL, STEP, Sharing package and Open in Bambu Studio

standards.insertNote: Seats 1 mm deeper than the insert, bosses with at least 2 mm of wall.
supportFree: Edges facing the bed get a 45° chamfer instead of a fillet
Bridges up to 10 mm, ledges up to 1.5 mm, wider ones become a 45° slope
Lying holes above about 10 mm get a teardrop or flat roof
Snap fits at about 1.4 % strain, with a warning above 2 % for PLA
checks: Walls of at least two lines, 0.9 mm with a 0.4 mm nozzle
Overhangs past your material’s angle, as a hint
At least 25 mm² on the bed
Gaps between parts tighter than the push fit

bento.title: Pull it apart
bento.text: Exploded views along the directions the parts go together, and sections along any axis or flat face.
bento.alt: An enclosure, its lid and a screw pulled apart

bento.title: Laid out on the plate
bento.text: Every part on its print face, nested on the bed of your printer, with parts that do not fit marked.
bento.alt: An enclosure, its lid and a board laid out on a print bed with its size

bento.title: Watch it go together
bento.text: The assembly plays step by step in the right order, sub-assemblies first, set by the assistant or proposed from the geometry.
bento.alt: The assembly of an enclosure halfway, with the named steps beside it

bento.title: Versions you can compare
bento.text: Saved before every request. Compare any of them with now.
bento.alt: The versions dialog comparing a named version with the current design

bento.title: Sketch the sizes
bento.text: Draw it on squared paper and type 40, Ø 8 or R 3. The assistant builds from them.
bento.alt: The sketch sheet with typed dimensions and an M3 hole label

bento.title: Start from a photo
bento.text: It asks for the one size that sets the scale. It never guesses from pixels.
bento.alt: The assistant asking for the length of a box shown in a photo

bento.title: Pick model and effort
bento.text: Per chat. With a Claude plan you see how much you have used.
bento.alt: The assistant menu with Claude Code, ChatGPT, local models, model and effort

bento.title: Build around real parts
bento.text: Import STEP and IGES as editable bodies, STL, 3MF and OBJ as meshes.
bento.alt: A housing built around an imported circuit board

bento.title: Projects and templates
bento.text: Every design is a folder you can see. Start from a box, clip or holder.
bento.alt: The start page with templates and project tiles

privacy.title: Your files stay yours
privacy.text: Projects are plain folders on your computer, sign-ins stay in the Windows credential store, and the app sends no telemetry. No account, no cloud of its own.

privacy.title: Your model, your choice
privacy.text: Use your Claude or ChatGPT subscription, or keep everything on your machine with a local model.

models.localNote: PartBuddy finds local servers on this computer and offers only models that can call tools and have at least 16K context.
